newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's Aznar seeks support for NATO integration.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Aznar seeks support for NATO integration.

text.p: Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar opened contacts on Thursday to clinch parliamentary support for Spain's full integration into NATO.

The government's spokesman confirmed that Aznar, who held talks with opposition Socialist leader Felipe Gonzalez, would meet various party leaders to discuss Spain's entry into the alliance's military structure.
"Before the end of the year, the corresponding proposal will be sent to parliament," spokesman Miguel Angel Rodriguez told reporters.

Spain, a member of the 16-nation alliance but not part of its military command, says it will integrate fully in NATO on condition that it can host a NATO command controlling access to the Mediterranean and all of Iberia.
Aznar said earlier this month he detected "a wide consensus" backing the government's push for full integration. Spain joined the alliance in 1982 and decided in a referendum in 1986 to stay in.
